reason: E2 shows Mo is a beta stabilizer with solid solution strengthening in Ti alloys, but neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence that Mo forms fine intermetallic precipitates in a Ti-Ni-primary HEA, that such precipitates improve creep resistance, or that 5–10 at% is the optimal range to avoid embrittlement. The key precipitation and strengthening mechanism is unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Mo is a beta stabilizer in Ti alloys and provides solid solution strengthening
Refractory elements like Mo improve mechanical properties in Ti and Ni superalloys
Mo addition can promote formation of intermetallic precipitates in a Ti-Ni HEA matrix
Fine, thermally stable Mo-rich precipitates will hinder dislocation motion at high temperature
5–10 at% Mo addition will not cause embrittlement or coarse precipitates
